### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.comment

### Description

Hello. First of all, thanks for such a good plugin. I love it. In fact, you have a collection of awesome plugins. You have put so much work on them, it is unbelievable!

Now about this issue itself, you see, I have started using mini.comment a few months ago I believe, and there is one thing that sometimes bugs me. I wish we could have different options for `ignore_blank_line` regarding the comments and the text objects.

I have been running a local change on mini.comment that adds a small if/else at `lua/mini/comment.lua`, inside the **MiniComment.textobject** function, that checks first for `config.options.ignore_blank_line_textobject` (I invented this option name) and, if that is **nil**, uses the standard `config.options.ignore_blank_line`.

This way, I can have `ignore_blank_line` set to **true** but on text objects I can make it behave as **false** as long as I put in my config the `ignore_blank_line_textobject` key.

The fallback to the normal `ignore_blank_line` seemed very reasonable and would keep the plugin working if you do not configure the new option. In fact, the default value of the new option should probably be **nil** so the plugin just uses the normal `ignore_blank_line_textobject` by default.

If you agree with this change, I'm happy to make a fork and open a PR.

That would need some documentation change, type comments, the config setup/apply functions, probably. I haven't checked them very well yet, but I would in case of a PR.

Thanks again for the plugins! (:

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion and kind words!

Could you please show a small example of a workflow you are trying to achieve and the basic reasoning behind it? Like a small section of lines, sequence of keys of type, and the expected behavior with why you think it is better.

Imagine a lua file:

```lua
-- Comment line 1

-- Comment line 2

local function add(n)
  local result = n + 1

  return result
end
```

If I set `ignore_blank_line` as **true** and I try to comment the whole function, I get this:

```lua
-- Comment line 1

-- Comment line 2

-- local function add(n)
--   local result = n + 1

--   return result
-- end
```

Which is what I want, leaving the blank line uncommented.

But then if I try to do something involving the textobject, for example if I place the cursor on top of the first comment and try to delete it, I will delete both Comment lines:

```lua
-- Comment line 1<CURSOR IS HERE>

-- Comment line 2


local function add(n)
  local result = n + 1

  return result
end
```

This becomes this:

```lua
<CURSOR IS HERE>
local function add(n)
  local result = n + 1

  return result
end
```

If I flip the `ignore_blank_line` to **false**, it works like I want when I delete/uncomment the textobject:

```lua
<CURSOR IS HERE>
-- Comment line 2

local function add(n)
  local result = n + 1

  return result
end
```

But now the comment action will comment the blank line inside the function:

```lua
-- local function add(n)
--   local result = n + 1
--
--   return result
-- end
```

I have found I prefer setting this option to **false** given that I must choose between these two options only, but sometimes I do wish that I could make the comment action have `ignore_blank_line` as **true**, but the textobject have it as **false**.

So inside MiniComment.textobject, instead of this:

```lua
  local ignore_blank_line = config.options.ignore_blank_line
```

I made this:

```lua
  local ignore_blank_line
  if config.options.ignore_blank_line_textobject ~= nil then
    ignore_blank_line = config.options.ignore_blank_line_textobject
  else
    ignore_blank_line = config.options.ignore_blank_line
  end
```

So now I could have different config options for these two actions (comment/uncomment and textobject).

I see, thanks for explaining.

The main logic behind how `ignore_blank_lines` handles textobject is that it should be able to uncomment with `gcgc` what was commented before with `gc` (in Visual mode or via an operator). Allowing different `ignore_blank_lines` for operator and textobject breaks this. So I don't think it is a good idea to add this kind of configuration.

The behavior described here is already possible to have with 'mini.comment' like this:

```lua
require('mini.comment').setup({ options = { ignore_blank_line = true } })

local my_comment_textobject = function()
  vim.b.minicomment_config = { options = { ignore_blank_line = false } }
  MiniComment.textobject()
  vim.b.minicomment_config = nil
end
vim.keymap.set('o', 'gc', my_comment_textobject)
```

It will remap `gc` in Operator-pending mode (for textobject) to temporarily use `config.options.ignore_blank_line = false`. Unfortunately, this is not something that will be taken into account if any change around `textobject()` will be made. But in reality I don't think there is anything in the future that would break this code. Hope this helps.

It is true that separating the logic breaks this, but this behaviour is one of the two things that made me wish I could separate them. I had something similar to this in a project I work on (it was a ruby file, but it is irrelevant):

```lua
-- Some documentation code (with an actual blank line after it)

local function something(x)
  local something = x + 1
  return x
end
```

if I comment the function via some operator and then try to uncomment with textobject, it uncomments the documentation comment.

The other situation that made me wonder I could separate them was two comments separated by a whitespace, they were unrelated, but deleting one deleted the other one as well.

Arguably these are problems on how the comments were made on that project. On the first example I would have the same problem anyways if the comment didn't have the blank line before the function, even on my sugested config, and the second is just unfortunate position of comments.

I guess we can't actually have everything, but to keep the old behaviour, one could just leave the new suggested option as nil.

But alas, I understand perfectly why you made your plugin behave like this and I understand why it is not desirable to allow the user to break it. I thank you for taking your time to answer this and share a workaround!

I didn't know about vim.b.minicomment_config, but I loved it. I was doing my own monkey patch version that was mutating MiniComment.config and MiniComment.textobject, but your version looks a lot cleaner. Thanks very much 🙏

title: mini.comment: Allow different options for ignore_blank_line on comments and text objects
